terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Three orthographic-like turn-sheet views constrain exterior proportions. Perspective is weak; hidden electronics and hinge internals remain inferred.

objectClass.notes: Three orthographic-like views establish the exterior workstation. Hidden electronics, monitor hinge stops, keyboard switches and mouse internals remain inferred.

reasoning: Five independently recognizable appliances form one workstation silhouette.
Keycaps and ventilation perforations require dense repeated systems; monitor hinge and animated screen/input states require an action-ready hierarchy.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Compound hard-surface set with articulated support, multiple I/O panels and repeated keys/vents.

detailInventory.note: Each observed identity detail maps to a named component or material feature.

details.description: Wide rounded cream monitor bezel around a recessed dark display.
Real rounded monitor rim catches a continuous highlight.
Screen is dark when off and becomes the dominant emissive computer interface when powered.
Five-petal pink flower mark centered on monitor rear shell.
Pink square rear mount plate separates the shell from the stand column.
Rear-leaning pink stand column with cream inner highlight strip.
Two-stage cream and pink rounded monitor base.
Tall cream tower shell with rounded corners and four pink feet.
Pink top cap overlaps tower shell with a horizontal seam.
Five-petal flower badge on tower front.
Vertical pink front I/O strip stands proud of the cream shell.
Large circular power button, status aperture and two rectangular USB cavities.
Vertical tower side-panel split remains visible in profile.
Side ventilation field forms a regular rounded-hole grid.
Rear has separate narrow and wide dense ventilation arrays.
Rear I/O column contains circular and rectangular socket cavities.
Bottom rear IEC-like power inlet sits beside a recessed service panel.
Keyboard has a cream rounded wedge shell and pink inset deck.
Independent cream/pink keycaps form six rows with a long pink spacebar.
Mouse uses a pink continuous arch over a cream lower shell.
Mouse center split separates buttons and carries a small wheel slot.
Power LED, screen boot glow, cursor/window changes and cooling cue act in one 5.2 second powered sequence.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Front, side, back and three-quarter renders preserve the five-piece workstation silhouette and reference proportions.
Monitor, stand, tower, keyboard and mouse remain separately named, pickable and explodable assemblies.
Monitor bezel/screen, tower top/I-O/vent systems, keyboard key matrix and mouse shell split remain readable at catalog scale.
The 5.2-second powered action unmistakably reads as a computer boot and input cycle, and stop returns every animated property to its exact initial value.

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.

Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.

Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Clay front preserves monitor-left/tower-right composition, monitor clearance, keyboard foreground and independent mouse silhouette.
Monitor, rear mount, leaning column and two-stage base remain volumetric in front, back and three-quarter clay captures.
Tower height/depth and rounded top/feet read as a separate upright mass; micro I/O is intentionally not judged in clay.
Keyboard wedge, stepped key field and arched mouse remain separate foreground silhouettes.

visualEvidence.notes: Also reviewed side, back and three-quarter clay captures; no planar collapse.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Clay review proves the monitor, tower, keyboard and mouse volumes. Pixel IoU is not authoritative because the reference is a portrait turn-sheet composition and the browser uses one persistent 3D layout.

featureReviews.notes: Bezel rails, screen, rear shell, mount plate, column and base are distinct named attached parts.
Tower shell, top cap, front I/O strip, rear panel, service cover and power inlet remain separable.
The 6x8 side field and two rear fields are independent repeated systems rather than painted texture.
Keyboard shell/deck/key groups/spacebar and mouse lower shell/top/buttons/wheel use independent hierarchy nodes.

visualEvidence.notes: No floating attachment is visible; structural coverage reports 38/38 with zero errors or warnings.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Back and three-quarter views verify separate monitor mount/stand, tower rear carrier, dual vent grids, I/O sockets, keyboard groups and mouse shell/button hierarchy.

featureReviews.notes: Rounded monitor, tower, keyboard and mouse proportions hold in front/back/three-quarter and non-degenerate orbit views.
True monitor thickness, rounded shell, bezel recess and leaned support avoid a flat-card read.
Tower corner radii, cap overlap, feet and front/rear panel relief are readable.
Vent perforation fields retain depth cues from side and rear views.
Six key rows, long spacebar, keyboard lip, mouse arch and wheel slot preserve identity.

visualEvidence.notes: Rounded bevels and independent relief remain visible at catalog scale.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Front preserves identity-defining proportions; side/back/three-quarter prove true thickness. Multi-angle diagnostic reports no degenerate view.

featureReviews.notes: Cream, Sakura pink and dark-screen zones reinforce the five-part silhouette.
Cream shell, dark glass, pink mount/column and cream inset remain visibly distinct.
Cream tower, pink cap/panels, dark port cavities and rubber feet preserve reference zones.
Cream/pink key distribution and pink-over-cream mouse split match the SAKURA palette.

visualEvidence.notes: No raw reference texture is tiled onto flat-color plastic; reference-derived channels remain independent evidence.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Five important material crops passed extraction confidence 0.854-0.909. Browser review confirms cream, pink, glass and cavity zones remain separated under neutral lighting.

featureReviews.notes: Warm key, cool fill and pink rim separate pale forms without clipping the silhouette.
Bezel, shell thickness, mount and base retain edge highlights and contact shadow.
Tower cap and panel bevels remain legible; port cavities retain dark value.
Side and rear holes remain dark and readable under the neutral review lighting.

visualEvidence.notes: Lighting is project-consistent SAKURA review lighting rather than a photometric copy of the turn-sheet.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Front provides neutral palette evidence; three-quarter supplies grazing bevel response; back proves dark vent/I-O retention and contact grounding.

featureReviews.notes: Power press and cyan LED lead into screen boot, desktop/window reveal, moving cursor, key presses, mouse click/wheel and cooling rotation.
Small bounded screen tilt originates at the named hinge and resets exactly.
Front power control and rear inferred cooling state remain anchored to the tower.
Independent active key, spacebar, button and wheel pivots provide readable input-device action.

visualEvidence.notes: No whole-object shake is used; every cue targets a purpose-specific pivot, material state or screen layer.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Explicit powered-state capture shows screen UI and cyan LED. Programmatic verification proves key depression 0.11, mouse click -0.09 rad, wheel/fan rotation, signal=1, then exact property reset and signal=0.

featureReviews.notes: Optimization preserves all macro silhouettes and named assemblies.

visualEvidence.notes: Optimization changed keycap segment density only; macro silhouette and identity details remain present.
